title: Streaming personal data to a child endpoint without compliant child-data handling safeguards
description: Because the recipient is a child user, the stream and its associated metadata may constitute children's personal data and require heightened legal and policy safeguards. If the service sends identifiers, behavioral data, or content-linked metadata without appropriate minimization, transparency, parental authorization where required, retention limits, or child-specific protections, the flow may violate applicable child-privacy obligations.
assumptions: Assumes the service is subject to child-privacy requirements and that the stream includes personal data or metadata linked to the child.
uncertainty_note: Nc.2 is directly supported by the retrieved context; applicability depends on jurisdiction and exact data included in the stream.

title: Excessive disclosure of child browsing data to the AI recommendation engine
description: The planned flow sends child browsing data from the childprofiles collection to the AI recommendation engine. If the engine receives raw or overly granular browsing histories, identifiers, timestamps, or full event logs beyond what is strictly necessary for generating recommendations, this constitutes avoidable disclosure of children's personal data within the system.
assumptions: Assumes the recommendation function could be implemented with minimized, aggregated, pseudonymized, or feature-extracted inputs rather than full browsing records.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for a data-minimization/over-disclosure branch; the retrieved context confirms Dd applies to DataStore->Process flows but does not provide the exact subtree citation.

title: Inference of sensitive child attributes from browsing data
description: Browsing data can allow the AI recommendation engine to infer sensitive or special-category information about a child, such as health concerns, emotional state, religion, sexuality, vulnerabilities, or developmental traits. Even if such attributes are not explicitly stored in the source collection, this flow enables their derivation during profiling and recommendation.
assumptions: Assumes browsing data contains sufficiently rich behavioral signals and the AI engine performs profiling or feature extraction for personalization.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort; applicability of inference risk is strong given AI profiling on child browsing data.

title: Secondary use of child browsing data for AI profiling beyond user expectations
description: Using child browsing data in an AI recommendation engine may be incompatible with the original context in which the data was collected, especially if users or guardians would reasonably expect storage for service operation but not automated profiling or model-driven personalization. This creates an unawareness risk about how the child's data is used.
assumptions: Assumes notices, consent flows, or parental explanations do not clearly and specifically disclose AI-based recommendation/profiling use.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; the threat is grounded in likely lack of transparency/expectation mismatch for planned AI use.

title: Potential incompatibility of AI recommendation use with children's-data compliance requirements
description: Processing child browsing data for AI recommendations may violate applicable privacy obligations if there is no valid legal basis, no age-appropriate transparency, insufficient parental authorization where required, or if profiling of children is restricted. The planned flow therefore raises a non-compliance risk tied to purpose limitation, data minimization, and children's privacy protections.
assumptions: Assumes the system handles children's personal data and the AI recommendation purpose may require additional safeguards or permissions under applicable law/policy.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-effort because the retrieved context does not include the Nc subtree; the compliance concern itself is well supported by the scenario.

title: Unnecessary disclosure of browsing data to third-party advertisers
description: The planned flow sends users' browsing data from the recommendation engine to external advertisers. This is an explicit disclosure of personal data across the system boundary and may violate data-minimisation if the advertisers do not strictly need the full browsing data for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Browsing data is personal data or can reasonably be linked to an identifiable user or device; advertisers are separate third parties outside the system boundary.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimisation structure; retrieved context confirms Dd applies to Process->ExternalEntity flows but does not provide the exact subtree id.

title: Cross-context linkability via shared browsing data
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers can enable those advertisers to link a user's activity in this system with profiles, identifiers, or observations from other services, making the user's actions across contexts linkable.
assumptions: Advertisers possess other identifiers, cookies, device fingerprints, or partner datasets that can be correlated with the disclosed browsing data.
uncertainty_note: Applicable threat type is strong for this flow, but the exact tree-node id is an informed estimate because the retrieved context only gives type-level applicability.

title: Identifiability of users from browsing data shared with advertisers
description: Browsing histories, page visits, timestamps, and associated metadata can make a user identifiable directly or indirectly when combined with advertiser-held data. The disclosure may therefore expose user identity even if direct identifiers are omitted.
assumptions: The shared dataset contains sufficiently granular events or metadata to permit singling out or re-identification when combined with third-party data.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; identifiability clearly applies, but the retrieved context does not include the detailed subtree mapping.

title: Detectability of user activity by third-party advertisers
description: The transfer itself can reveal that a particular user or device interacted with certain content, products, or categories. Even limited event data may allow advertisers to detect that a user performed specific actions within the system.
assumptions: The flow includes user-, session-, device-, or event-level data rather than only fully aggregated anonymous statistics.
uncertainty_note: Threat applicability is plausible for event-level browsing-data sharing; exact subtree id is best judgement.

title: Sharing browsing data with advertisers may exceed user consent or reasonable expectations
description: Sending browsing data to third-party advertisers is a secondary use and disclosure that may not be covered by valid, specific, and informed consent, or may conflict with user expectations and purpose limitation commitments.
assumptions: Users have not explicitly consented to advertiser sharing for this purpose, or consent is bundled/insufficiently specific.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance is strongly plausible for planned advertiser sharing, but depends on the actual legal basis, notices, and consent design.

title: Users may be unaware that browsing data is sent to third-party advertisers
description: If the recommendation engine discloses browsing data to advertisers without clear, timely, and understandable notice, users may not be aware of who receives their data, for what purpose, and with what consequences.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-product disclosures are absent, unclear, delayed, or too generic to make the sharing understandable.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness depends on the transparency mechanisms actually implemented; exact tree-node id is approximate.

title: Excessive retention or storage of government ID images
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data. Storing full images in the file system may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary for authentication or verification purposes, especially if images are retained after verification or stored at higher fidelity than needed.
assumptions: Assumes the system may persist full ID images in backend/uploads/ rather than immediately extracting only required attributes or deleting images after verification.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; exact subnode may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Unintended disclosure of ID images from broadly accessible upload storage
description: Writing government ID images into a generic uploads directory increases the risk that sensitive images become accessible to unintended internal parties, co-hosted components, backup operators, or through misconfiguration of file serving paths. This constitutes avoidable disclosure of personal data to parties beyond those strictly required.
assumptions: Assumes backend/uploads/ may be a shared or operationally accessible storage location and not a tightly isolated evidence vault.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate; grounded in avoidable explicit/implicit disclosure during storage and onward operational access.

title: Storage of government ID images may be unnecessary or disproportionate
description: Persisting raw government ID images may violate data-minimization and storage-limitation expectations if the purpose can be fulfilled by storing a verification result, extracted attributes, or a short-lived token instead of the full image. This creates a non-compliance risk for privacy requirements governing necessity and proportionality.
assumptions: Assumes there is no demonstrated legal or operational necessity to retain the full image after verification.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is best judgement; applicability depends on jurisdiction and documented retention/legal basis.

title: Government ID images enable strong identifiability of the data subject
description: A stored government ID image directly contains strong identifiers and often additional attributes such as full name, date of birth, document number, and photo. Persisting these images in the datastore makes the subject readily identifiable from the stored content.
assumptions: Assumes the uploaded images are readable and linked to user records or otherwise retrievable in context.
uncertainty_note: Identifiability is inherent to government ID images; exact subnode id may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: JWT in localStorage enables cross-context linkability
description: Persisting a JWT in browser localStorage creates a stable client-side identifier/token that can be reused across sessions and application contexts on the same origin. If multiple pages, scripts, or components access the same token, user actions and sessions can be linked together more easily than necessary.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains a stable subject/session identifier or is reused long enough to correlate activity across visits.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgement because the retrieved context gives applicable threat types for Process->DataStore but not the detailed LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability.

title: JWT contents may identify the user when stored client-side
description: A JWT often contains claims such as subject, email, username, tenant, or roles. Storing it in localStorage means any script running in the origin can read those claims, making the user directly or indirectly identifiable from the stored token.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is readable by client-side scripts and contains identifying or quasi-identifying claims, as is common for bearer tokens.
uncertainty_note: Detailed subtree id is approximate; applicability is strong if the JWT is not opaque and contains identity claims.

title: localStorage persistence increases risk of unauthorized disclosure of the JWT
description: localStorage is accessible to JavaScript in the origin and persists beyond the current browser session. If malicious or compromised scripts execute in the page, the stored JWT can be read and exfiltrated, disclosing authentication material and any privacy-relevant claims it contains.
assumptions: Assumes realistic risk of XSS, third-party script compromise, browser extension access, shared-device access, or other client-side compromise.
uncertainty_note: This is a strong privacy threat for this flow, though the exact tree node id is best-judgement.

title: Persistent JWT storage may exceed user expectations or consent
description: Storing an authentication token in localStorage can retain login state and associated identity data longer than users expect, especially across browser restarts. If users are not clearly informed or given meaningful control over this persistence, the storage may violate consent, preference, or data-minimization expectations.
assumptions: Assumes the application does not clearly disclose token persistence/retention behavior or provide suitable controls such as logout invalidation and storage minimization.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on the application's notice, consent, and retention design; included because the flow explicitly stores a persistent auth token client-side.

title: Parent can link child history across time and contexts
description: The flow returns child history for review, which inherently aggregates multiple events or records about the child. If the history includes stable identifiers, timestamps, categories, or cross-context records, the parent can link separate data items into a richer profile than needed for the immediate purpose, revealing additional sensitive inferences about the child.
assumptions: Assumes the returned history spans multiple events/sources or contains recurring identifiers or quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context confirms Linking applies to Process->ExternalEntity flows but did not provide a more specific node id.

title: Excessive disclosure of child history to parent
description: Sending child history to the parent may disclose more personal data than necessary for the review purpose, such as detailed event logs, sensitive categories, or information about third parties. This creates a risk that confidential aspects of the child's activities or status are exposed beyond what is proportionate.
assumptions: Assumes the history payload may contain detailed or sensitive records rather than a minimized summary.
uncertainty_note: Specific threat-tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context only established applicability of Identifiability/Information disclosure to this interaction type.

title: Parent can infer sensitive attributes from child history
description: Even if the transmitted history omits explicit sensitive labels, patterns in activities, timestamps, frequency, or categories may allow the parent to infer sensitive information about the child, such as health, behavior, beliefs, relationships, or vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Assumes the history contains sufficiently granular behavioral or contextual data to support inference.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary depending on the nature of the history data.

title: Child may be unaware that full history is disclosed to parent
description: If the system retrieves and sends the child's history to the parent without clear visibility to the child, the child may not detect that their past records are being reviewed. This reduces transparency about who receives the data and when.
assumptions: Assumes the child is a relevant data subject and is not notified or otherwise able to observe this disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on product design and whether child-facing transparency mechanisms exist.

title: Secondary use of child history beyond the child's expectations
description: Child history collected for operational or educational/safety purposes may be repurposed for parental review in a way the child does not reasonably expect. The flow can therefore undermine predictability about how previously collected data will be used.
assumptions: Assumes the original collection context did not clearly communicate parental review of the full history.
uncertainty_note: This depends strongly on the stated purpose and notices presented at collection time.

title: Disclosure of child history to parent may exceed consent or legal basis
description: Providing the child's history to the parent may be non-compliant if the disclosure exceeds the granted consent, the child's rights, age-dependent autonomy rules, custody constraints, or data-minimization obligations. The privacy risk is especially acute where only part of the history should be shareable with a parent.
assumptions: Assumes there may be jurisdictional, age-related, or role-based limits on parental access to the child's records.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on legal context, parental authority model, and platform policy; exact subnode selected by best judgement.
